q: Which statement about the audit risk model is most accurate?
o: Audit risk equals inherent risk plus control risk less detection risk
Detection risk is assessed from the entity control environment
Control risk falls as substantive procedures become more extensive
RMM combines inherent and control risk; detection risk is inverse
why: Inherent and control risk exist independently of the audit and together form RMM; the auditor manages only detection risk through nature, timing and extent of procedures.

q: An auditor assesses control risk as low for the revenue cycle but performs no tests of controls. Under SA 330 the consequence is that:
o: Control risk must be taken at maximum for those assertions
Detection risk may be raised on the low control risk assessment
Prior year control testing may be relied on for several years
Substantive analytics alone become sufficient for the revenue cycle
why: Reduced substantive work is permitted only where tests of controls evidence operating effectiveness; without such testing the assurance must be obtained substantively.

q: Which characteristic would NOT by itself indicate a significant risk under SA 315?
o: High subjectivity in measuring an accounting estimate at year end
A non routine related party deal outside the ordinary course
High volume routine sales through a well controlled system
Accounting complexity with recent changes to the reporting rules
why: Routine high volume transactions subject to systematic processing sit lower on the inherent risk spectrum; significant risks stem from subjectivity, complexity, uncertainty, change or susceptibility to bias and fraud.

q: Where the auditor plans a wholly substantive approach to a significant risk, SA 330 requires that:
o: Substantive analytics alone suffice where the data is predictable
Controls must nevertheless be tested in every reporting period
The procedures must include tests of details for that risk
The procedures may be done at interim with no roll forward work
why: SA 330 states that a substantive only approach to a significant risk must include tests of details, and substantive procedures for significant risks are directed to the period end rather than interim alone.

q: Risks of material misstatement at the financial statement level are best addressed by:
o: Increasing sample sizes for the specific account balances affected
Testing operating effectiveness of application controls per cycle
Obtaining further written representations from management
Overall responses on scepticism, staffing and unpredictability
why: FS level risks are pervasive and relate to the control environment and management integrity, so SA 330 calls for overall responses; sampling and application control testing address assertion level risks.

q: The control environment is weak but the auditor identifies a well designed reconciliation control over trade payables. The most appropriate conclusion is:
o: A weak environment may undermine the specific control
The specific control is reliable regardless of the environment
Control risk must be set at maximum for the entire audit
ITGC testing is unnecessary because this control is manual
why: The control environment underpins the other components, so pervasive weaknesses cast doubt on specific controls; this does not mechanically force maximum control risk everywhere.

q: The SA 315 requirement to understand internal control relevant to the audit obliges the auditor to:
o: Test operating effectiveness of all controls in the five components
Accept management process narratives as control documentation
Evaluate design and determine implementation beyond inquiry
Assess control risk below maximum for every material balance
why: Design and implementation must be evaluated by combining inquiry with observation, inspection or tracing a transaction; operating effectiveness testing is a separate SA 330 decision.

q: Building unpredictability into the selection of audit procedures is required mainly because:
o: SA 330 requires audit team members to be rotated every three years
Management aware of the usual pattern can conceal fraud better
It lowers the inherent risk attaching to the affected accounts
It substitutes for the mandatory testing of journal entries
why: Predictable audit patterns make concealment easier, so SA 240 and SA 330 require an element of unpredictability; it does not change inherent risk and never replaces journal entry testing.

q: Where controls tested in a prior audit are unchanged, SA 330 permits reliance on that earlier testing subject to which limit?
o: Reliance for up to five years without any further retesting
Reliance indefinitely once management confirms no change
Reliance only where the control is automated and ITGCs work
Retest at least every third audit; significant risks each year
why: The rotation limit is three years for unchanged controls with a portion tested each period, but controls mitigating a significant risk must be tested in the current period.

q: Which item would most likely be assessed as a significant risk requiring specific audit attention?
o: Depreciation computed by the fixed asset module at standard rates
Allocating consideration across a multi element contract
Statutory dues computed directly from the payroll master data
Routine utility expenses supported by matched vendor invoices
why: Significant risks involve high subjectivity, complexity or judgement, which multi element allocation clearly does; the other items are systematic, routine and objectively supported.

q: Why does the distinction between inherent risk and control risk matter in practice?
o: Inherent risk can be reduced by the auditor but control risk cannot
Only control risk has any bearing on the determination of samples
It shows where exposure arises and drives different responses
Inherent risk is only at statement level and control at assertion
why: Neither can be changed by the auditor, but separating them clarifies whether the exposure comes from the nature of the item or from control failure; both can arise at either level.

q: Before relying on a substantive analytical procedure over payroll expense, SA 520 and SA 330 require the auditor to:
o: Assess data reliability and set the acceptable difference first
Set the tolerable difference after comparing with the recorded sum
Perform it only where control risk is assessed at the maximum
Restrict it to balances falling below performance materiality
why: Reliability of the data, suitability for the assertion, precision of the expectation and a predetermined acceptable difference are the preconditions; setting the threshold afterwards defeats the test.

q: Which statement about risk assessment procedures under SA 315 is correct?
o: They alone give sufficient appropriate evidence for the opinion
Analytical procedures may not serve as risk assessment procedures
Observation and inspection are barred as risk procedures
They must be supplemented by further audit procedures
why: SA 315 is explicit that risk assessment procedures provide the basis for identifying risks but not sufficient evidence for the opinion; inquiry, analytics, observation and inspection are all valid.

q: A company implements a new ERP three months before year end. The most appropriate audit response is to:
o: Rely on legacy system testing for the year as processes are alike
Assess control risk as low given the embedded automated controls
Test controls for each period and address data conversion risk
Restrict all control testing to the post implementation period
why: Controls differ across the two periods so each must be tested in its own period, and migration creates completeness and accuracy risk over converted balances; embedded controls are not effective merely by existing.

q: SA 330 requires substantive procedures irrespective of the assessed risk of material misstatement for:
o: Every single account balance exceeding performance materiality
Only those assertions for which controls were not tested at all
Only accounts affected by an identified significant risk
Each material class, balance and disclosure in the statements
why: The standard mandates substantive procedures for every material class, balance and disclosure regardless of assessed RMM, because controls alone cannot give complete assurance.

q: Performing substantive procedures at an interim date increases which risk, and what response does SA 330 require?
o: Detection risk for the remaining period; cover it by procedures
Inherent risk; reperform the whole interim sample at the year end
Control risk; controls must then be tested only at the year end
Sampling risk; the interim sample size must be doubled at year end
why: Interim testing leaves the intervening period uncovered, so substantive procedures or a combination with control testing must cover the remaining period; full reperformance is not required.

q: Which is the best example of an assertion level response to the risk of management override of controls?
o: Assigning an engagement partner with greater industry experience
Increasing the frequency of engagement team discussions on risk
Testing journal entries, especially non standard year end ones
Obtaining a management representation covering control override
why: Journal entry testing focused on unusual and period end entries is the specific procedure SA 240 requires for override; team composition and discussions are overall responses and a representation is not evidence.

q: Inventory valuation at a plant is assessed as high risk because of slow moving stock. The most responsive procedure is to:
o: Attending the physical count and observing the count procedures
Confirming inventory held by third parties for the entity
Testing cut off of goods received notes around the year end
Testing ageing and net realisable value against later prices
why: Ageing, NRV testing and challenge of the provision address valuation directly; count attendance and confirmations address existence and rights while cut off addresses completeness and occurrence.
